what_its_for: This medicine is used to relieve mild to moderately severe pain. It contains two medicines that work together: acetaminophen (a common pain reliever) and codeine (an opioid pain reliever that works in the brain to change how your body feels and responds to pain).
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you. You may take it with or without food, but taking it with food or milk can help prevent an upset stomach. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the liquid form, carefully measure your dose using the measuring device that comes with your medicine — never use a regular kitchen spoon, as this can give you the wrong amount. Do not take more than prescribed, and do not take it more often than directed.
dosing: Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to take and how often. A typical adult dose is 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain. Do not take more than 6 tablets in 24 hours. Never take more than 4,000 mg of acetaminophen total per day from ALL sources (including other products like cold medicines that contain acetaminophen). Taking too much acetaminophen can seriously damage your liver. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and you are taking this medicine on a regular schedule, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you are taking this medicine only when you need it for pain (not on a schedule), take it when you need it and do not worry about a missed dose.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in a safe place out of reach of children and pets — this medicine can be very dangerous or life-threatening if taken by a child. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet unless the label says to do so. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of leftover medicine, such as using a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol can increase your risk of liver damage from acetaminophen and can cause dangerous drowsiness with codeine. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you — it can cause drowsiness and dizziness. Do not take other medicines that contain acetaminophen (such as many cold, flu, or sleep medicines) without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, as too much acetaminophen can harm your liver. Avoid taking sedatives, sleeping pills, anti-anxiety medicines, muscle relaxers, or other opioids unless your doctor has told you it is safe, as combining these with codeine can cause serious breathing problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: slow, shallow, or stopped breathing; extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up; confusion or unusual behavior; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); dark urine or very light-colored stools; severe stomach pain; skin rash, blisters, or peeling; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; or if you feel you cannot stop taking this medicine. Call your doctor if your pain is not being controlled or if you develop constipation, nausea, or vomiting that bothers you.
when_it_works: This medicine usually begins to relieve pain within 30 to 60 minutes after you take it. The pain-relieving effects typically last about 4 to 6 hours. This medicine is meant to be used for short-term pain relief. Do not use it longer than your doctor recommends.
special_populations: Children: Codeine is NOT recommended for children under 12 years old due to the risk of serious breathing problems. It should also be avoided in children under 18 who have had their tonsils or adenoids removed. Teens and young adults (12–18): Use only if prescribed by a doctor, and watch closely for breathing problems. Older adults (65+): Use with extra caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and drowsiness, which can increase the risk of falls. Pregnant women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine during pregnancy. Using codeine near the end of pregnancy may cause withdrawal symptoms in the newborn. Breastfeeding mothers: Do NOT use this medicine while breastfeeding. Codeine passes into breast milk and can cause dangerous breathing problems in nursing babies. People with liver or kidney problems: Use with caution and follow your doctor's dose instructions carefully, as these conditions can affect how your body processes the medicine.
